system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Great-Power Competition Meets Financial Stress
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system in which resurgent great-power rivalry, regional wars, and technology-security frictions are colliding with fragile financial and energy markets. Strong US macro data and a global bond sell-off are amplifying policy uncertainty while simultaneous kinetic escalations (Middle East, Ukraine) and supply‑chain moves (rare earths, oil deals) create cross‑domain contagion. Policymakers juggle crisis management, diplomatic shuttle diplomacy, and emergent AI governance amid persistent migration, cyber, and industrial-security pressures.
system_description.scope: Interstate strategic competition and diplomacy among major and regional powers; ongoing kinetic conflicts and crisis escalation (Ukraine, Middle East, Iran-related strikes); global financial markets (bond yields, currency moves, capital flows); energy and commodity markets and shipping chokepoints; critical‑materials and tech supply chains (rare earths, AI, semiconductors); migration, cyber/sabotage incidents, and international institutional responses.
system_description.super_system: The Anthropocene global socio-technical-economic system: the planetary network of states, markets, technologies and environmental constraints within which geopolitics and globalized commerce operate.
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and central-bank policy transmission
Energy and commodity flows (oil, gas, shipping chokepoints)
Technology and critical‑materials governance (AI safety, rare earths, semiconductors)
Regional security clusters (Middle East conflicts; Russia–Ukraine–Europe complex)
evidence_headlines: U.S. payrolls rose 162,000 in August, much more than expected; unemployment rate at 4.1%
Global bond sell-off deepens amid inflation fears
U.S. launches further strikes on Iran as conflict flares up
China rare earth firms halt some US shipments over geopolitical worries, sources say
Russian drone strikes Ukraine’s security service headquarters

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed respectively by differing blocs, remain locked in a large‑scale territorial war that is shifting frontlines, defence integration and Eurasian security architectures.

variables.name: U.S.–Iran military confrontation
variables.description: The United States and Iran (and their regional partners) are engaged in a persistent tit‑for‑tat military confrontation that is recalibrating regional deterrence, naval posture and alliance calculations.

variables.name: U.S.–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting technology, trade and diplomatic leadership—from AI governance and export controls to summit diplomacy—shifting trajectories of economic interdependence and strategic decoupling.

variables.name: Global bond market shock
variables.description: Major economies and central banks are confronting a synchronized bond sell‑off driven by stronger data and inflation fears, shifting borrowing costs, monetary policy paths and fragile financial‑stability dynamics worldwide.

variables.name: Global energy supply realignment
variables.description: Energy producers, purchasers and state actors are reconfiguring supplies through alternative deals, storage shortfalls and production shifts, driving price volatility and geopolitical leverage in energy markets ahead of winter.
